parameters.content:
## Bot Review · Outcomes (Phase 0)

Every 30 minutes: POST LP-MCP `/api/bot-feedback/jobs/outcomes`.

**What it does.** LP-MCP reconciles `bot_outcomes` for every fingerprinted bot send in the last 8 days that is not yet final — did the lead reply within 24h, did an appointment get created within 7 days, did they opt out within 24h. The signals are read from the HL cache and matched in code; LP and HL are never joined.

**Why a cron and not a webhook.** The three signals arrive on their own schedule (an inbound now, a booking on Thursday), so the only way to catch them is to look again. 30 minutes is the handoff's cadence (§5.1) and keeps a reply's outcome fresh enough for a same-day review.

**A 200 with `ok: false` is not a failure.** LP-MCP answers 200 for conditions Mark has to fix by hand — `sql/103_bot_feedback_core.sql` not applied yet, or `HL_SUPABASE_URL` unset — so the cron does not go red for something it cannot do anything about. Read `data.reason`. A red execution means LP-MCP itself was unreachable or threw.

**Stale HL cache is handled, not failed.** If HL messages or appointments last synced more than 2h ago, outcomes are still computed but recorded `source_fresh: false` and NEVER marked final, so a quiet cache is never mistaken for a quiet lead. Watch `data.source_fresh` in the execution output.

**Before activating:**
1. `sql/103_bot_feedback_core.sql` applied in the LP Supabase SQL editor.
2. LP-MCP deployed with the Phase 0 code.
3. **Attach the bearer credential to the HTTP node by hand.** Create a **Bearer Auth** credential named `LP MCP Bearer Auth` with value = LP-MCP's `MCP_AUTH_TOKEN`, then select it on `POST outcomes job`.

   This file deliberately ships the node with NO credential. Naming one without an id made n8n bind the node to an unrelated bearer credential (`Supabase Highlevel MCP`) on the first import — which would have sent the HL Supabase service key to LP-MCP every 30 minutes. Unbound fails loudly and sends nothing; that is the safer default.

   After attaching it, pin the credential's **id** into this file and open a PR, because `scripts/deploy-to-n8n.py` pushes `nodes` wholesale and the next deploy would otherwise clear the binding again.

**Shipped inactive.** Mark imports and activates.

nodes.name: Every 30 min ET
nodes.notes: Every 30 minutes, around the clock. Timezone America/New_York is set on the workflow so this and every other Bot Review cron share the business clock (handoff §0/§6); for a fixed half-hourly interval the zone makes no difference to the firing times, but it does to how the executions read.

nodes.name: POST outcomes job
nodes.notes:
120s timeout: one run reconciles up to BOT_OUTCOMES_BATCH_LIMIT (500) fingerprints and makes three batched HL reads. neverError is deliberately OFF — unlike the capacity-ranker watchdog there is no repair branch to route a non-2xx into, so a genuine LP-MCP failure should fail the execution and be visible in the execution list. The expected soft conditions (SQL not applied, HL credentials unset) come back as 200 with ok:false and do not go red.

CREDENTIAL IS NOT SET HERE ON PURPOSE. The first cut of this file named one ("LP MCP Bearer Auth") without an id; n8n could not match it and silently bound the node to an unrelated httpBearerAuth credential instead — "Supabase Highlevel MCP", which would have sent the HL Supabase service key to LP-MCP on every run. An unbound node fails loudly and sends nothing, which is the safe default. Attach the credential in the n8n UI, then pin it here BY ID so future deploys stop re-binding it (this file's `nodes` are pushed wholesale on every deploy).

meta.note: Bot Review Phase 0 (handoff §6). Requires LP-MCP to expose POST /api/bot-feedback/jobs/outcomes, which ships in the LP-MCP Phase 0 PR. Shipped INACTIVE: activate only after sql/103_bot_feedback_core.sql is applied and LP-MCP is deployed, or every run returns ok:false with reason 'missing_relation'.
